rationale: Across the primary defining literature (Janssen et al., 2022; OMIM #620450), individuals with autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder 73 (T4NDD) present with generalized, nonspecific facial dysmorphic features rather than a highly penetrant, pathognomonic facial gestalt. While broad facial dysmorphism is noted in 7/8 individuals (87.5%), OMIM #620450 explicitly classifies these as 'nonspecific dysmorphic facial features', and discrete individual dysmorphic signs (e.g., arched eyebrows, epicanthal folds, thin upper lip) lack uniform penetrance across probands (<75%), precluding diagnosis or phenotypic segregation based on any single craniofacial anomaly alone.

evidence.text: OMIM entry 620450 defines the phenotypic spectrum of autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder 73 based on Janssen et al. (2022), characterizing the dysmorphology as nonspecific dysmorphic facial features rather than an invariant recognizable gestalt.

new_directions.question_text: Does computer-aided 3D facial phenotyping (e.g., GestaltMatcher or Face2Gene) identify a latent, statistically significant facial signature for TAF4-related NDD despite the absence of an obvious discrete single facial anomaly?
new_directions.rationale: When individual dysmorphic signs appear heterogeneous or nonspecific by manual dysmorphology assessment, multi-dimensional geometric deep learning models can often extract composite spatial signatures that distinguish the syndrome from other neurodevelopmental disorders.

new_directions.question_text: Do missense variants in specific functional domains of TAF4 (e.g., the TAFH or histone-fold domain) cause distinct craniofacial patterns compared to truncating putative loss-of-function variants?
new_directions.rationale: The initial cohort described primarily de novo pLoF variants; assessing missense or domain-specific mutations in larger worldwide cohorts will establish whether true phenotypic substructure exists.
